ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure, the AC power supply u1 is applied to the transformer primary winding N1, and the wattmeter W is connected in the primary-side input circuit, so it measures the primary-side input active power. On the right side there are two mutually independent secondary windings N2 and N3; N2 is connected to resistor R1 through switch S1, and N3 is connected to resistor R2 through switch S2, so the two secondary-side loads are independent resistive loads controlled by switches. Reasoning: When both S1 and S2 are open, there is no load on the secondary side, and the wattmeter reading is 4 W, which according to the problem statement is taken as the no-load iron loss P_fe = 4 W. When both S1 and S2 are closed, the secondary-side voltages U2 = 20 V and U3 = 30 V, and R1 = 10 Ω and R2 = 30 Ω. The output powers of the two resistive loads are respectively P_R1 = U2^2/R1 = 20^2/10 = 40 W, P_R2 = U3^2/R2 = 30^2/30 = 30 W, so the total output power P_out = 40 + 30 = 70 W. At this time the wattmeter reading is the input power P_in = 80 W, and the total transformer loss is P_loss = P_in - P_out = 80 - 70 = 10 W. The total loss consists of iron loss and copper loss, so the copper loss under load is P_cu = P_loss - P_fe = 10 - 4 = 6 W.

planner_metadata.text_role: Use the given numerical data U1=200 V, R1=10 Ω, R2=30 Ω, open-circuit wattmeter reading 4 W, loaded secondary voltages U2=20 V and U3=30 V, and loaded wattmeter reading 80 W.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the wattmeter is on the primary side, while closing S1 and S2 connects pure resistive loads to the two secondary windings. Use the open-switch test to identify the fixed core-loss contribution as 4 W at U1=200 V. In the loaded test, remove this fixed contribution from the wattmeter reading: 80-4=76 W is the active power associated with load supply plus copper heating. From the closed-switch secondary voltages, compute the actual external load powers: 20^2/10=40 W in R1 and 30^2/30=30 W in R2, total 70 W. The remaining active power is winding copper loss: 76-70=6 W.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Open-circuit primary real power at rated voltage represents the excitation/core-loss branch power. At the same U1, subtracting this fixed active power from the loaded input leaves the real power going to secondary loads plus winding copper losses. Resistive load powers are computed with U^2/R.
